items.title: Carney Says No Hurry on Trade Deal If US Won’t Offer Good Terms
items.author: Stephanie Hughes
items.content: <article>Prime Minister Mark Carney said he won’t rush a trade agreement with the US if the terms aren’t in Canada’s best interests, and suggested he expects his country will still be in President Donald Trump’s crosshairs after the US midterm elections.</article>

items.title: Refugees From Ukraine’s Besieged Oleshky Are Returned to Safety
items.author: Kollen Post
items.content: <article>Refugees from the besieged southern town of Oleshky have returned to free Ukrainian territory and reunited with family members.</article>

items.title: Trump’s Board of Peace Petitions Italy for Gaza Police Support
items.author: Donato Paolo Mancini
items.content: <article>US President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace formally asked Italy to provide advisers from the police, firefighters and the carabinieri corps to help build a new security force for the Gaza Strip, according to letters seen by Bloomberg News.</article>

items.title: US Embassy Warns of Mass Casualty Threat at Moscow Museum
items.author: Ros Krasny
items.content: <article>The US embassy in Moscow said it was “aware of a credible threat of a mass casualty event” on Saturday at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve in Moscow, and was coordinating with Russian authorities on a response.</article>

items.title: Israel’s Election Leaves Netanyahu in Limbo
items.content: <article>Bloomberg Israel Bureau Chief Ethan Bronner tells Bloomberg This Weekend that neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor the opposition has a clear path to forming a government after Israel’s election, potentially setting up difficult coalition negotiations or another vote. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Bronner discusses Netanyahu’s political durability, increased Arab voter participation and how another conflict with Iran could alter the coalition calculus. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Why Kalshi, Polymarket Odds Don't Mimic Midterm Elections 2026 Polls
items.author: Carolyn Silverman, Ella Feldman and Leonardo Nicoletti
items.content: What may seem like contradictory numbers are, in fact, just two ways to capture a similar picture.

items.title: Bolsonaro Leaves Brazil After Rejecting Election
items.content: <article>Bloomberg Brazil Country Chief Filipe Pacheco tells Bloomberg This Weekend how Flávio Bolsonaro left Brazil for the US after refusing to recognize Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s election victory, as Bolsonaro faces multiple investigations in Brazil. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Pacheco explains Bolsonaro’s circuitous journey to Miami, his pledge to lead the opposition from the US and how investors are assessing Lula’s surprise comeback. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Midterm Fight Comes Down to the Final Days
items.content: <article>Bloomberg Balance of Power co-host Joe Mathieu joins Bloomberg This Weekend to break down the final days of campaigning before the midterms, including President Donald Trump’s late push and the House and Senate races that could determine control of Congress. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Rep. Meeks Puts Affordability Atop Democrats’ Agenda
items.content: <article>House Foreign Affairs Committee Ranking Member Gregory Meeks tells Bloomberg This Weekend that affordability would be Democrats’ top priority if they take control of the House, alongside restoring health-care benefits and conducting oversight of the Trump administration. Speaking with host David Gura, Meeks says companies involved in importing Russian diesel could face congressional scrutiny and predicts Hakeem Jeffries would become speaker if Democrats win the majority. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: The AI Backlash Uniting Voters
items.content: <article>Artificial intelligence is becoming a political issue for the first time in this year’s midterms, with much of the voter backlash focused not on the technology itself but on the data centers needed to power it. Communities from Michigan to Texas are raising concerns about electricity costs, water use and the broader impact of AI on jobs and local economies. Former House Speaker Paul Ryan says data centers have become a proxy for wider fears about AI. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Publicidad política en español cae antes de elecciones de EE.UU.
items.author: María Paula Mijares Torres
items.content: Las elecciones de medio término van camino a ser las más caras de la historia, pero los anuncios políticos en español se desploman pese al creciente peso del voto latino.

items.title: Midterm Elections 2026: Spending surge is leaving out Spanish-language ads
items.author: María Paula Mijares Torres
items.content: <article>The US midterm elections are on track to be the most expensive ever, with ad spending set to top $11 billion, but the share being directed toward Spanish-language advertisements is shrinking dramatically, even with Latino voters seen by both parties as a critical swing group.</article>

items.title: Investors Brace for Post-Midterm Policy Shifts
items.content: <article>Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Government Analyst Nathan Dean tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the midterm results could reshape congressional oversight while the Trump administration continues pursuing deregulation across banking, crypto and other industries. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Dean explains what investors should watch in energy, AI, banking and trade, including the potential for further tariffs and changes that could encourage regional bank consolidation. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: The Affordability Crisis Shaping US Elections
items.content: <article>The US economy remains resilient, but many Americans are still struggling with the cost of housing, health care, groceries and other necessities. Former House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Kevin Brady and Willett Advisors Chairman & CEO Steven Rattner explain why the gap between strong economic data and household finances has made affordability one of the defining issues of the midterm elections. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: US Starts at ‘Basically Zero’ in Building Cheap Military Drones
items.author: Andrew Martin and Jen Judson
items.content: <article>At a manufacturing plant near Salt Lake City with a big American flag on the wall and work stations crammed with tools and parts, dronemaker   Vector Defense Inc. is in expansion mode.</article>

items.title: Cost of Living Looms Over the Midterms
items.content: <article>Bloomberg Economics Economic Statecraft Lead Chris Kennedy tells Bloomberg This Weekend that higher costs for gasoline, groceries and housing are weighing on voters and putting pressure on parts of the coalition Donald Trump assembled in 2024. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Kennedy explains how affordability concerns are playing out in states including Michigan, Iowa and Texas and how control of Congress could shape economic policy after the midterms. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Ukraine Strikes Bashneft Refineries as Russia Attacks Power Grid
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>Ukraine’s drone forces struck a complex of refineries deep within Russia, even as Kyiv and other parts of the country struggled to restore electricity following overnight Russian strikes on energy infrastructure.</article>

items.title: Iran Threatens Wider US Strikes Even as Talks Make Progress
items.author: Patrick Sykes and Eric Martin
items.content: <article>Iran’s Supreme Leader ordered his top military commanders to prepare for renewed confrontation with the US and Israel and expand Tehran’s options for retaliation, even as his top diplomat signaled progress in diplomatic talks.</article>

items.title: US Midterms: Trumpism May Already Be in Decline Worldwide
items.author: Alan Crawford
items.content: <article>US elections from Alaska to Maine will reverberate globally next week, as midterm voting promises to diminish a president who has strong-armed the world.</article>

items.title: Polish President Holds Crisis Talks as Court Standoff Grows
items.author: Maciej Martewicz
items.content: <article>Polish President Karol Nawrocki scheduled emergency consultations with parliamentary parties on Saturday to “restore constitutional order” as an escalating standoff at the country’s top court threatened to spark a political crisis.</article>
